newsitem.title: USA: Fed seeks rivals to Crane for currency - report.
newsitem.headline: Fed seeks rivals to Crane for currency - report.

text.p: The Treasury Department is considering offering financial incentives to the U.S. subsidiaries of foreign papermakers if they will compete against Massachusetts-based Crane & Co. for the U.S. currency contract, the Boston Globe reported Friday.
Crane, the nation's sole supplier of currency paper for more than 100 years and one of the largest manufacturers in western Massachusetts, could not be immediately reached for comment.

But the newspaper reported officials of the Dalton, Mass., papermaker said they would be forced to lay off workers and idle specialized machinery if Crane lost its contract with the U.S. government. The contract is valued at $75 million a year.
Crane employes 1,400 workers and about 200 of them produce nine truckloads weekly of customized cotton and linen paper for the U.S. Bureau of Printing and Engraving.

Treasury officials did not return phone calls immediately, but the Globe reported the department has put a draft solicitation on the Internet encouraging paper makers to bid for the work and offered subsidies in unspecified amounts for start-up costs and equipment plus a four-year contract for inducement.
The aim is to build enough competition into the market so that over time the government will recoup its subsidies, the newspaper said.
